_description: Security exceptions for the CI self-check gate. This file suppresses false positives that arise when the security-mcp tool scans its own source code. It is NOT used for user project gate runs.

exceptions.justification: security-mcp is a developer CLI security scanner tool, not an application server. Controls requiring auth middleware, MFA enforcement, audit logging infrastructure, egress controls, and network segmentation are not applicable to this tool's architecture. The tool itself enforces these controls in user project code — it does not implement them internally.

SLSA provenance is generated by GitHub Actions via 'npm publish --provenance' and is attached to the npm package registry entry. The tool does not produce .intoto.jsonl files in .mcp/attestations/ because provenance is managed at the npm publish layer, not at the repo layer.

These findings come from the REMEDIATION_MAP in src/mcp/server.ts, which contains intentional 'before' example code patterns (e.g., sslmode=disable, md5 hashing, console.log(req.body), postgresql://user:pass@host) used to show developers how to fix vulnerabilities. The patterns appear in string literals as educational examples, not as actual application code. GRAPHQL_INTROSPECTION_ALWAYS_ON, GRAPHQL_NO_COMPLEXITY_LIMIT, CRYPTO_GCM_NONCE_REUSE_RISK, CRYPTO_SHA_USED_FOR_PASSWORD, CRYPTO_INSECURE_RANDOM_IDENTIFIER, TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED_DISABLED, JWT_MISSING_EXPIRY, and JWT_ALG_NOT_LOCKED also match REMEDIATION_MAP examples, security checklist strings in server.ts, and .mcp/baselines/ stored scan data — none are in live application code. SQL_INJECTION and SQL_INJECTION_CONCAT match the REMEDIATION_MAP 'before' SQL example. WEAK_CRYPTO_HASH and HARDCODED_DB_URL_OR_API_KEY are additional IDs generated by the new deep-scan checks for the same REMEDIATION_MAP false-positive class. HARDCODED_IP_ADDRESS matches 127.0.0.1/localhost literals in tests and defaults. security-mcp has no HTTP server, no user sessions, and no cookies — these checks do not apply to its architecture.

Runtime dependencies (execa, fast-glob, picomatch, zod) have low OpenSSF Scorecard scores due to minimal OSSF project infrastructure (no Scorecard workflow, branch protection). These are mature, widely-used packages with no known critical CVEs. Replacement would introduce more risk than retention. Risk accepted pending upstream scorecard improvements. DEPENDENCY_CONFUSION_RISK for @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is expected — this is a public npm package from Anthropic; no private registry override is needed.

The CI self-check environment has an empty scanner config (.github/security-tools-ci.json) because external scanners (gitleaks, semgrep, osv-scanner) are not installed in the GitHub Actions runner for this self-check step. The tool's own built-in checks cover the equivalent detections. Users are expected to have these tools installed in their own environments.

False positives from patterns matched in non-application files: DANGEROUSLY_SET_INNER_HTML matched in .mcp/baselines/ JSON data (a stored scan result, not code); SSRF_GUARD_REQUIRED matched 'undici-types' in package-lock.json (a type-definition package, not an HTTP client usage); IAM_OVERPRIVILEGED matched 'Action: *' in README.md documentation showing an anti-pattern; PUBLIC_EXPOSURE_RISK matched '0.0.0.0/0' in README.md explaining what to avoid; JWT_ALG_NONE_ACCEPTED matched a checklist item in server.ts that documents JWT security requirements as a string literal, not actual jwt.verify() code; WEB_HEADERS_MISSING and SSRF_USER_URL matched HTTP calls in src/cli/ that have explicit hostname allowlist checks (ALLOWED_SKILL_HOSTS, ALLOWED_BINARY_HOSTS) validating URLs before every fetch — all callers pass only hardcoded constants or pre-allowlisted URLs. security-mcp is a CLI/MCP scanner tool with no HTTP server surface, no JWT auth, and no IAM policies.

COMMAND_INJECTION in src/cli/onboarding.ts and src/cli/update.ts — spawnSync/execSync are called with fixed command arrays derived from constants and an internal command builder, never from user-supplied strings. REDOS_USER_REGEXP in src/repo/search.ts — new RegExp() is intentional: the call is the final step of compileUserRegex() which enforces a 256-char limit, a nested-quantifier detection check, and lets Node.js throw SyntaxError for invalid patterns; the CWE-1333 risk is mitigated by these guards at the call site. REQUIRE_NON_LITERAL in src/cli/index.ts — require(resolve(__dirname, '../../package.json')) uses __dirname which is a compile-time constant, not user input; this pattern reads the bundled package.json for the version string. ARTIFACTS_NO_THREAT_MODEL and ARTIFACTS_NO_SBOM are project-level artifact gaps, not code-level vulnerabilities; they are tracked in CI (not pre-commit) and are covered by the self-scan-provenance and self-scan-control-evidence exceptions for the CI gate. POSSIBLE_SECRET in src/ci/pr-gate.ts matches process.env.SECURITY_GATE_POLICY with a file-path default — the default value is a config path, not a secret. GIT_HISTORY_SECRET matches JWT keyword in skills/stride-pasta-analyst/SKILL.md documentation and generic-api-key pattern in server.ts REMEDIATION_MAP — neither are actual secrets. CI_EXCEPTIONS_IN_LOCAL_SCAN is a meta-finding triggered when CI exception files are applied in local scans; intentional for the self-scan workflow where CI exceptions are the canonical exception set. AUDIT_LOGGING_DISABLED matched text in .mcp/baselines/ stored scan data, not actual application config. SECRET_DIST_NOT_SCANNED is expected — dist/ is generated from TypeScript source that is scanned; no secrets are introduced at build time. GRAPHQL_CIRCULAR_FRAGMENT_RISK is a new detection for circular GraphQL fragments; security-mcp has no GraphQL server. BASELINE_REGRESSION for PCI_REQ6_SECURE_SYSTEMS is a false positive in file_by_file pre-commit mode — that control depends on osv-scanner/trivy tooling that is not in scope for staged-file scanning; the control is satisfied in full CI runs.

False positives from two sources: (1) SKILL.md files in skills/ that contain intentional vulnerability examples for educational/detection-testing purposes (e.g., skills/aws-penetration-tester/SKILL.md contains `http_tokens = optional`, `authorization_type = NONE`, `is_multi_region_trail = false` as attack patterns for pentesters to recognize — not infrastructure config). (2) .mcp/agent-runs/ JSON output files that contain finding IDs and evidence strings from previous CISO Orchestrator runs — scanning stored findings data inevitably matches patterns those findings describe. CRYPTO_NO_FORWARD_SECRECY was matched in a stored crypto-findings.json agent output, not in application TLS configuration. security-mcp has no cloud infrastructure, no Lambda functions, no CloudTrail, and no Azure resources.

The repo's own .github/workflows/security-gate.yml triggers on 'pull_request' (NOT 'pull_request_target') and references secrets.SECURITY_POLICY_HMAC_KEY. GitHub does not expose repository secrets to pull_request runs from forks, so a fork contributor cannot read this secret; only same-repo branch PRs receive it. The reference is optional/no-op (the workflow documents the gate functions without the key) and exists to sign-verify the policy on trusted same-repo PRs. The detection is a conservative true-positive by rule (secrets.* present in a pull_request workflow) but is not exploitable here. Suppressed only in the repo-local self-scan; .github/ is not shipped in the npm package, so downstream CI_FORK_SECRET_EXPOSURE detection is unaffected.

The repo's .github/workflows/security-gate.yml passes GITHUB_TOKEN (via env) to gitleaks/gitleaks-action, a non-actions/* third-party action. gitleaks-action v3 REQUIRES GITHUB_TOKEN to scan 'pull_request' events; without it the step errors and the entire security-gate fails on every PR (and the failure skips the Trivy step, cascading to a 'trivy-results.sarif not found' upload error). The exfiltration risk flagged by CI_SECRET_TO_THIRD_PARTY_ACTION (CWE-522) is mitigated exactly as the finding's own requiredActions prescribe: the action is pinned to a full 40-char commit SHA (e0c47f4f8be36e29cdc102c57e68cb5cbf0e8d1e) and the workflow scopes permissions to 'contents: read' + 'security-events: write' only (no contents/pull-requests/packages write), so only the minimal low-privilege GITHUB_TOKEN is handed over. Suppressed only in the repo-local self-scan; .github/ is not shipped in the npm package (package.json files: dist/, prompts/, skills/, defaults/), so downstream detection is unaffected.

Self-scan false positives from the v1.4.0 deep crypto and business-logic checks matching security-mcp's own outbound HTTPS client code in src/cli/update.ts and src/mcp/orchestration.ts. (1) CRYPTO_MISSING_CERT_PINNING flags plain https.get() calls (update.ts:67, update.ts:116, orchestration.ts:322) — these are standard outbound GETs from a CLI to public infrastructure (npm registry, release/skill manifests), not high-value API endpoints; certificate pinning is not applicable to a CLI making ordinary HTTPS requests, and pinning public CA-rotated endpoints would break the tool. (2) BIZ_BULK_OP_NOT_TENANT_SCOPED (CRITICAL) matches the substring 'destroy(' in req.destroy()/req.setTimeout(()=>req.destroy()) calls on Node's https.ClientRequest object (update.ts:83/98/126/132, orchestration.ts:329/334) — these abort an in-flight HTTP request on size/timeout limits; they are NOT database updateMany/deleteMany/bulkWrite operations. security-mcp is a CLI/MCP scanner tool with no database, no tenants, and no multi-tenant data model, so tenant-scoping does not apply. Suppressed only in the repo-local self-scan; .github/ is not shipped in the npm package (package.json files: dist/, prompts/, skills/, defaults/), so downstream detection of real DB bulk ops and pinned high-value endpoints in user code is unaffected.

Self-scan false positives from the v1.3.5 documentation, in which CHANGELOG.md, README.md, and docs/WIKI.md describe the detection rules the gate ships and therefore quote the very patterns those rules match. (1) WEB_OPEN_REDIRECT matches the prose example `res.redirect(req.query.url)` used to explain the rule (CHANGELOG.md:65, and the rule name repeated in README.md/WIKI.md). (2) IAC_AWS_PASSROLE_PRIVESC_CHAIN matches the phrase `iam:PassRole` in the 1.5.0 emerging-cloud description (CHANGELOG.md:196). (3) AI_INVISIBLE_UNICODE_INJECTION matches the warning emoji ⚠️ (U+FE0F variation selector) used in a CHANGELOG section heading and in the tool's own authentication-preamble UI string (src/mcp/auth.ts) — a legitimate emoji, not smuggled instructions. (4) VIBE_PUBLIC_ENV_HOLDS_SECRET and (5) VIBE_DEBUG_MODE_ENABLED match the rule NAMES and their example strings where the CHANGELOG/WIKI enumerate the vibe-coding rule set. All five are descriptive documentation of security-mcp's own detectors, not vulnerabilities in shippable code. Suppressed only in the repo-local self-scan; .github/ is not shipped in the npm package (package.json files: dist/, prompts/, skills/, defaults/, README.md, LICENSE — the CHANGELOG and docs/WIKI.md are not packaged), so downstream detection of these classes in user code is unaffected.

src/tests/corpus/*.corpus.ts intentionally embeds realistic vulnerable code as string-literal true-positive fixtures for the per-rule detection corpus added in this release (src/tests/corpus/runner.ts) — the same false-positive class already excepted for REMEDIATION_MAP's own before/after examples under self-scan-remediation-map. Originally covered the 2-rule web-hardening.corpus.ts smoke test (OPEN_REDIRECT/POST_LOGIN_OPEN_REDIRECT/WEB_HARDCODED_SESSION_SECRET) plus DYNAMIC_IMPORT_NON_LITERAL and MONETARY_FLOAT_ARITHMETIC from src/tests/run.ts's corpus-file loader; extended for the Wave 2 fan-out that added a corpus file per check module (35 modules, 507 cases); extended again here after a full non-diff-scoped self-scan (SECURITY_GATE_MODE=file_by_file over every git-tracked, non-ignored file, matching CI's own invocation) surfaced additional corpus-triggered ids that a diff-scoped pre-commit check hadn't covered — including the 5 CRITICAL/HIGH ones (K8S_INGRESS_NGINX_SNIPPET_INJECTION, INFRA_DB_NO_DELETION_PROTECTION, INFRA_ECR_NO_SCAN, INFRA_ECS_HOST_NETWORK, INFRA_GCP_DEFAULT_SERVICE_ACCOUNT) that would have failed the next full CI run. Every id in this list cites only files under src/tests/corpus/ (SSH keys, JWT/webhook/registry secrets, SQL/NoSQL/command injection payloads, weak-crypto configs, business-logic and DLP fixtures, Terraform/Helm/ArgoCD/Kubernetes IaC snippets, etc.) as the RuleCase.positive.content string literal each rule is specifically authored to trigger — never live application code. Two ids (GRAPHQL_VERBOSE_ERRORS, VIBE_SOURCEMAPS_IN_PROD) additionally cite CHANGELOG.md and docs/WIKI.md, where pre-existing release notes and the rule catalog describe these rules using their own trigger literals (e.g. WIKI.md's rule table lists 'productionBrowserSourceMaps: true' as the pattern VIBE_SOURCEMAPS_IN_PROD detects) — the same doc-describing-the-rule-it-triggers class already excepted elsewhere in this file for other ids (self-scan-doc-and-data-false-positives, self-scan-v15-v16-fixtures-and-teaching-skills). DYNAMIC_IMPORT_NON_LITERAL's reasoning is unchanged: the imported path in src/tests/run.ts is built from a fixed repo-relative directory (dist/tests/corpus) plus a filename returned by readdirSync of that same trusted directory, filtered to *.corpus.js — never user- or network-controlled input; a static import list is not possible because corpus files are added over time without code changes elsewhere. MONETARY_FLOAT_ARITHMETIC is unchanged: it cites a tpRate/fpRate percentage formatted with .toFixed(2) in the same file — a detection-rate ratio in [0,1], not a monetary amount. Also covers ids formerly listed under two now-deleted entries whose original justification (fixtures/skills paths, or v1.5.0/v1.6.0/v1.6.1 fixtures) no longer matches why they fire: a full non-diff-scoped self-scan (SECURITY_GATE_MODE=file_by_file over every git-tracked, non-ignored file) showed self-scan-fixtures-and-cloud-controls's and self-scan-v15-v16-fixtures-and-teaching-skills's remaining live ids now reproduce exclusively via src/tests/corpus/*.corpus.ts (the Wave 2 corpus fixtures) — the fixtures/ and skills/ paths those entries were written for are now excluded outright by CI's SECURITY_GATE_IGNORE, so citing them as the reason would be inaccurate. Two ids (IAC_TF_MODULE_GIT_UNPINNED_REF, IAC_GCP_TOKEN_CREATOR_PROJECT_BINDING) instead cite docs/UPGRADE_BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md, which documents these rules using their own trigger literals — the same doc-describing-the-rule class as GRAPHQL_VERBOSE_ERRORS/VIBE_SOURCEMAPS_IN_PROD above.
